geographical_area: City of Rome and its urban speech community (Romanesco). The profile follows contemporary urban Romanesco as described by the Vocabolario del romanesco contemporaneo; Belli-era forms are used only for proverbs and quotations. Other Lazio varieties (Castelli Romani, Ciociaria, Viterbese, Reatino) are not covered.
linguistic_classification: Central Italian (Italo-Romance), Romanesco, the dialect of Rome; heavily Tuscanized since the 15th-16th centuries and forming a continuum with regional Italian of Rome.
orthographic_conventions: Modern popular dialect writing: apocopated infinitives with accent (magnà, annà, fà, dì, vedé), apostrophes for aphaeresis and truncation ('n, 'na, 'ndo, 'sto, so', mo', pe', co'), gli written j (fijo, moje, mejo), rhotacism of l before consonants (er, quer, sòrdi, vorta), -nd- > -nn- (quanno, monno), no written syntactic doubling outside quotations of Belli and Zanazzo, Lex Porena forms ('o, 'a, 'i, aa, dea) only sparingly at intensity 5.
description_en: Romanesco of Rome: article er/li, rhotacism (er, vorta, sòrdi), -nd- > -nn-, gli > j, apocopated infinitives (magnà, annà), nun for negation, 2sg subject te, je as universal dative, avecce for possession (c'ho, c'hai), ce sta for existence, progressive with stà a + infinitive, present tense preferred for the future, and a distinctly vulgar, deflating, ironic register. Voice: a detached, teasing speaker who urges with 'daje!'.
description_it: Il romanesco di Roma: articolo er/li, rotacismo (er, vorta, sòrdi), -nd- > -nn-, gli > j, infiniti tronchi (magnà, annà), nun per la negazione, te soggetto di 2a persona, je dativo universale, avecce per il possesso (c'ho, c'hai), ce sta per l'esistenza, progressivo con stà a + infinito, presente al posto del futuro e un registro marcatamente volgare, ironico e dissacrante. Tono: distaccato e sornione, che sprona con 'daje!'.

identifier_word.meaning_en: Roman discourse marker: 'come on! let's go!', 'OK, deal', and with e- ('e daje!') 'oh come on, not again'.
identifier_word.meaning_it: Segnale discorsivo romano: 'dai, forza, andiamo', 'd'accordo' e, preceduto da e ('e daje!'), 'uffa, di nuovo'.
identifier_word.attestation: Documented as dàje (1) in the Vocabolario del romanesco contemporaneo (letter D) and in Wiktionary; Belli writes it dàjje. The mode name is the authentic Roman form, not an academic name of the variety.

known_limitations: No native-speaker review yet: all example sentences are AI-illustrative, built on documented rules.
Romanesco is structurally close to Italian and has no standard spelling: the profile adopts one convention (accented infinitives, apostrophes) and lists alternatives.
Modern slang and many colloquial items rest on low-reliability popular sources (src-rom-intrepidguide, src-rom-elon) and on single dictionary entries; the VRC covers only the letter D.
Proverbs come mostly from Zanazzo (1886) and Belli (19th c.); their spelling uses written doubling, so the profile gives plain modern variants.
No Roman-specific blasphemies are documented from verified sources, so the profile generates none beyond one flagged idiom.
Lex Porena forms ('o, 'a, 'i, aa) are low register and attested sparsely; they are kept rare to avoid caricature.
